articleTitle: Fully 3D-Printed RFID Tags based on Printable Metallic Filament: Performance Comparison with other Fabrication Techniques
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: FDM (Fused Deposition Modelling) 3D printing emerged in the last few years as one of the most promising additive manufacturing techniques for fast prototyping. In this work, this technique is used to fabricate UHF (Ultra High Frequency) RFID (Radiofrequency Identification) flexible tag antennas, using a plastic-based conductive filament with copper inclusions, called Electrifi. A comparison with other prototypes with similar shape but fabricated through different and already investigated techniques [1] has been performed in terms of ease of use, processing time, cost, tag sensitivity, radiation pattern, and impedance. More specifically, 3D-printing technology for RFID tag fabrication is compared with inkjet printing, screen printing, wax-based deposition, and cutting plotter. The conductive properties of the antennas realized with the Electrifi filament, as expected, are lower than those of the antennas realized with the other techniques. Nevertheless, a slight degradation in terms of tag performances, is balanced by the extremely high versatility of the fabrication technique. Moreover, the capability to easily fabricate a fully 3D printable antenna, together with the possibility to print complex and not only planar geometries, pave the way to interesting and meaningful future developments.

articleTitle: SLM 3D-Printed Horn Antenna for Satellite Communications at X-band
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper presents a SLM (Selective Laser Melting) 3D-printed, circularly polarised horn antenna suited for satellite communications at X-band. As described in this paper, SLM 3D-printing is used to directly 3D-print the horn antenna in aluminium from a powdered metal bed as opposed to more indirect and imprecise methods found in literature, such as metallising plastic 3D-printed parts. Using this novel manufacturing technique, the entire antenna with stepped septum polariser is printed as one solid component. This ensures perfect alignment and electrical continuity between subcomponents and negates the need for any post-processing work before the antenna could be used. The unibody design of the antenna results in exceptional performance over the satellite communications receive band of 7.9 - 8.4 GHz, and maintains excellent performance over a much larger bandwidth of 7.5 - 11.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Active Multiport Subarrays for 5G Communications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: A novel hybrid beamforming architecture based on a phased array of active multiport subarrays is proposed for multi-user 5G applications. The subarrays have multiple simultaneous fixed beams which are smartly combined at the user locations with relatively large gains towards the intended co-frequency users and sufficiently low inter-user interference levels. The presented architecture has a wider angular coverage than the existing subarray-based hybrid beamforming schemes and reduces the signal processing complexity significantly as compared to the fully digital beamforming.

articleTitle: Indoor Body-to-Body LoRa Link Characterization
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This contribution examines the performance of LoRa in an indoor, body-centric IoT context. This was achieved by deploying custom-made wearable LoRa nodes, featuring a textile substrate-integrated-waveguide antenna, on the chests of test persons who walked around in a modern office environment, logging the strength of the link between them. Both the influence of the test person's bodies as well as the challenging environment, which includes large masses of reinforced concrete, are investigated. The measured channel characterization data illustrate the excellent performance achieved by combining the building penetration qualities of signals at sub-GHz frequencies and the high link budget of the LoRa modulation standard.

articleTitle: Frequency Reconfigurable and Radiation Pattern Steering of Monopole Antenna Based on Graphene Pads
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper presents a reconfigurable band of operation from 5G to 4G for radio frequency energy harvesting (RF-EH) in the different wireless communication bands. The designed antenna with steerable beam pattern based on tunable of the graphene pads. The proposed antenna consists of printed CPW-fed circular monopole shaped and five rectangular strips are added with equally separation angle 45<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>. These strips are connected with monopole by using graphene pads. The monopole antenna resonates at 5G applications extended from 3 GHz up to 7.8 GHz at -10 dB reflection coefficient with Omni-radiation pattern over the operating band without any bias voltage of the graphene pads. By applying the dc voltage to the graphene pad the rectangular strips are connected to the monopole and the designed antenna start to resonant from 1.8 GHz to 7.5 GHz to add the 4G wireless applications. The steering of the beam from 60<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup> to -60o according to the graphene pad that connect to the monopole. The graphene pad exhibits as variable resistance from almost short to open circuit with and without voltage bias, respectively. The designed antenna is simulated using High Frequency Structure Simulation (HFSS) Ansys ver. 19. The simulated equivalent circuit of the graphene is applied then reduced graphene oxide (RGO) pads are deposited to validate the results. Fabricated prototype is then used to experimentally validate the simulation results. Finally, Reflection coefficient and radiation pattern measurements and simulations are presented, good agreement between these results.

Author Keywords: energy harvesting (EH) and radiation pattern steering

articleTitle: Low Cost Ambient Backscatter for Agricultural Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In our days, the massive growth of Internet-of-Things related applications has required the design and fabrication of low-cost and low-power wireless sensors. The last decade, backscatter communication has been introduced as a cutting-edge technology that could address the above limitations. In high precision agricultural applications, the monitoring of plant-water-stress (PWS) is of high importance for smart sensing. Instead of the traditional ground soil moisture sensing, leaf sensing is an old technology, which is used for the detection of PWS. Considering the above topics, this work aims to mention the development of a novel sensor node/tag for environmental leaf sensing which uses backscattering communication over ambient frequency modulated signals (FM music signals). The work is based on our previous works [1], [2] and it is described how ambient backscatter technology could be exploited for the “one sensor/plant” concept in precision agriculture applications.

articleTitle: The Effects of the Trapezoidal Dipole Array Elements on Planar Log Periodic Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In this study, a planar log periodic trapezoidal dipole array antenna operating 2-6 GHz frequency range is designed. The simulations is performed in CST Microwave Studio (full-wave 3D EM solver) using Rogers 4003C substrate material from program library. In order to reduce antenna size, the antenna design with trapezoidal dipole shape is proposed. Iterative simulations are performed to obtain better voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) along the operating bandwidth. The effects of the trapezoidal dipole element are examined in terms of VSWR, radiation pattern and gain. Moreover, the designed antenna is fabricated and the manufactured antenna is measured using near-field measurement system. It can be concluded that the designed antenna will be useful for military or civilian applications.

articleTitle: Interference simulation between 5G and GSO–NGSO networks at 27-30 GHz range
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: The IMT-2020 networks, or the so-called 5G networks by industry, are the next technological evolution of mobile communications. These networks based on the 3GPP specifications over the Release 16 will be effective implemented on millimeter wave spectrum above 24.25 GHz. The candidate spectrum as defined by ITU-R are the frequencies bands ranging from 24.25 GHz to 66 GHz. Studies were made in order to define the portion of spectrum to be identified on the WRC-19. Although the 28 GHz band is not part of the WRC-19, actually this spectrum is identified for mobile applications in the ITU-R Radio Regulations. This paper presents the sharing studies with existing services in the 28 GHz band in adjacent channel and co-channel scenarios. These services have been used globally by satellite industry with products and services in the so-called Ka Band for the Earth-Space communications, known as the Fixed Satellite Service (FSS). Simulations were made with the SHARC (Simulator for Sharing and Compatibility Studies) software developed by Anatel and academy with the implementation of Rec. ITU M.2101, with essential parameters of the IMT-2020 technology. For the satellite networks, scenarios with Geostationary Satellite Orbit (GSO) and non-GSO (NGSO) parameters were also considered.

articleTitle: A Novel High-Temperature Stable Antenna with Omnidirectional radiation pattern
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Novel high-temperature stable antenna with reliable structure is presented in this communication. The antenna is excited by a coaxial line which can adapt high-temperature within 350 °C. The height of the antenna is only 0.26λ (where λ is the wavelength at the centre frequency). A parametric study is performed for providing practical design guidelines The simulation and measured results show that an impedance bandwidth for VSWR ≤ 2.0 from 2.1GHz to 4.8GHz was covered. Stable radiation pattern is found among the working frequencies. The antenna works stably at 350 °C with the protection of heat shield cover plate and demonstrates excellent heat-resisting property, while the surface temperature of the antenna reaches 280 °C.

articleTitle: A Multiobjective Genetic Algorithm for Analysis, Design and optimization of Antipodal Vivaldi Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In the this contribution, a Multi-Objective Genetic Algorithm (MOGA) was implemented to analyze, design and optimize several Antipodal Vivaldi Antennas (AVA) that are being used on Ground Penetration Radars (GPR) applications. This algorithm was implemented and used as an optimization tool in a commercial available software. Directivity, lower cutoff frequency (LCF), bandwidth and cross-polarization were the objectives to be optimized. For the use of the MOGA, the 3D model of the antenna is built in the simulator. Some of its parameters are defined as variables, as the dimensions and shape of the antenna (Individual) depend on the value that its parameters (Genes) take. This work proves to be simple and time saving tool to optimize parameters in a geometry changing system as GPR.

articleTitle: Two Types of High Gain Slot Array Antennas based on Ridge Gap Waveguide in the D-Band
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: The recent introduced ridge gap waveguide shows huge strengths in array antennas in millimeter and sub- millimeter wave frequencies. Generally, gap waveguide supplies contactless characteristics in order to avoid the good electrical contact between the different metallic layers. Therefore, the gap waveguide structures are relatively simple to be fabricated in Ka-, V-, W-bands. As is well known, the conductor loss increases rapidly versus frequency in millimeter wave and submillimeter wave frequencies. Thereby, the increasing conductor loss above 100 GHz affects the antenna gain. In this work, we compare two types of antennas in the D- band. The full cooperate feed array antenna is wide band, avoiding the offset of main beam. However, the number of T - junction power dividers rapidly increases. Thereby, it is necessary to design a T- junction power divider with ultra-low reflection for a big array in the D- band so that the gain of the big array antenna enhances. On the other hand, a series feed antenna array is also a choice in the D- band. The series feed structure has advantages of less power dividers, easy design. Nevertheless, it is unable to avoid the long line effect, narrow bandwidth and main beam offset. The comparison between two structures has been done in the D - band in this work.

Author Keywords: millimeter wave and slot array antenna

articleTitle: Miniaturized Pixel Antenna for Implantation on the ARGOS CubeSat 4U
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Today, the dimensions of wireless equipment are constantly decreasing; hence, embedded antennas are increasingly being miniaturized. For example, the emergence of nanosatellites called “CubeSats” requires design of antennas compatible with footprints divided by three or four compared to those of conventional satellites for the same operation. Due to their property of transverse evanescence [1] of the internal EM fields and their broadband nature [1], the “Pixel” antennas are good candidates for miniaturization. The antenna presented in this paper is designed to be used alone but usually such element is introduced in the ARMA (Agile Radiating Matrix Antenna), in which case it is referred to as a “Pixel” Antenna [4]. Thus, the objective of this paper is to design a miniaturized planar antenna for ARGOS beacon, implanted on a CubeSat 4U (20cm × 20cm); this antenna must make it possible to realize the Tx and Rx links in circular polarization in the UHF band.

articleTitle: A Compact Wearable Textile Antenna with Dual Band-Notched Characteristics for UWB Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper presents design and simulation analysis of a Compact Wearable Textile Antenna with Dual Band-notched characteristics for UWB applications. The antenna consists of a CPW fed semicircular radiator with two semicircular split ring resonators (SSRR). The antenna has a dimension of 43mm×40mm×2mm, designed on the leather substrate with dielectric constant 1.65 and a loss tangent of 0.02 and uses copper foil as conducting material. The frequency band-notched characteristics are achieved by inserting two semicircular split ring resonators (SSRR) on the patch of the antenna. The first notch band is obtained from 2.3 - 2.5GHz for Bluetooth application band and the second notch band is obtained from 3.3 - 3.7GHz for WiMAX (IEEE 802.16) application band. It is observed that the notch frequencies can be controlled by varying the widths of the slots, the distance between two semicircular rings and the two ends of the semicircular ring slot. The simulated frequency results show that the antenna has an impedance bandwidth of 1.8 - 10.7GHz and reflection coefficient less than -10dB, except the two eliminated bands to reject the Bluetooth application band at 2.4GHz and the WiMAX application band 3.3 - 3.6GHz. Ansys HFSS Electromagnetic simulator has been used for simulations and results are presented.

articleTitle: Capacity Based Optimization of Compact Wideband Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a framework for designing and optimizing compact wideband antennas using the Shannon capacity formula. We present a new single port Gamma matching network that enhances the system's spectral efficiency apart from satisfying the antenna's figures of merit. We provide an in-depth analysis of the designed antenna by using a circuit theoretic approach. To optimize the allocated power across the frequency range of interest, we implement the waterfilling method. Finally, we develop interesting insights on the importance of optimizing impedance matching networks from an information theoretic perspective.

articleTitle: UTD Human Body Models Comparison based on dual Motion Capture and Radio Measurements
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Nowadays, human body influence on communication channels attracts a lot of interest, especially for Wireless Body Area Networks (WBANs) and future fifth-generation (5G) communications systems. For this last application, Human Body Shadowing (HBS) will be one of the major causes of Non Line of Sight (NLoS) because of the use of millimeter waves (mmWaves). Thus, an accurate modeling of human body impact on wireless communications seems paramount.In this paper, the proposed deterministic model, based on Ray-Tracing (RT) and Uniform Theory of Diffraction (UTD), uses different human body models based on circular cylinder(s) and/or sphere. For the models comparison, the study accounts for an unprecedented measurement campaign based on both Motion Capture (MoCap) and radio systems working at a frequency of 2.4 GHz.

articleTitle: A Novel Filter Antenna for Base Station
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In this paper, a novel filter antenna for base station is proposed for decoupling. The filter antenna proposed in this paper opreates from 1680 to 2940MHz(does not include the filter band, 1920 to 1980MHz), which is consisted of three substrates, a reflector, and there are four resonator structures in the radiator or next to the feeding lines which could filter unwanted frequency band. In order to improve selectivity, two resonators could be used to jointly control one notched band. Further more, We use the method of filtering to realize decoupling. This method not only improves the isolation, but also ensures that the radiation pattern of the antenna is not affected.

articleTitle: Low Profile Wideband 3D Antenna for Roof-Top LTE Vehicular Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In this study, a low profile wideband 3D antenna for roof-top LTE vehicular applications is presented. The structure consists of folded metal sheets welded together building a geometry that allows covering two LTE bands: 700MHz-960MHz, 1700MHz-2700MHz. The shape and the size of the antenna allow to fit it under the shark-fin case, and thanks to the chosen material the production costs are low. Simulations and measurements have been performed taking into account two antennas working as a MIMO configuration. Both numerical and measurement results show good performances in terms of return loss, coupling and gain.

articleTitle: Automatized Solution for Over-the-Air (OTA) Testing and Validation of Automotive Radar Sensors
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: The growing importance of Radar solutions in automotive applications results in new standards to be met and more demanding performances to be assured. As such, Radar developers require testers capable of guaranteeing compliance with the specified criteria. This paper presents a preliminary approach to allow over-the-air (OTA) testing and validation of 76-77 GHz and 77-81 GHz Radar units in production lines, covering not only pass/fail conditions, but also determination of the Radar antenna array radiation diagrams (in azimuth and elevation) through a calibrated external power sensor. Preliminary measurements on an open environment test bench are shown for different Radar bandwidths (1 GHz and 4 GHz), illustrating the importance of a clean and shielded anechoic chamber environment as a baseline approach.

articleTitle: Multi-Protocol LoRaWAN/Wi-Fi Sensor Node Performance Assessment for Industry 4.0 Energy Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper describes the implementation of an end-to-end Internet of Things (IoT) solution, focusing specifically in the multi-protocol sensor node with LoRaWAN and Wi-Fi connectivity options (Pycom's FiPy). A performance assessment will be presented, addressing a comparison between the different protocols (LoRaWAN vs. Wi-Fi) in terms radio coverage, timing issues, among others. Further, it will be investigated the integration onto the sensor node of sensor/actuator circuit blocks for energy metering, supported on Microchip's ATM90E26 single-phase meter. This will provide a practical use case in the field of Industry 4.0, leading to preliminary insights for power quality monitoring.

articleTitle: A Mobile Terminal Leaky-Wave Antenna for Efficient 5G Communication
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: The millimeter-wave 37-43.5GHz band is proposed to provide the requested multigigabit-per-second (Gb/s) data rates for future 5G cellular communications [1]. As a total wireless-link gain of 37 dBi may be required, the mobile terminal antennas should provide 12 dBi gain -being the remaining 25 dBi for the base station antennas- [2], [3]. This high gain is linked to the synthesis of narrow directive radiated beam, which must somehow be scanned into space over a wide field of view (FoV), and thus satisfy the mobility and coverage conditions. Such high-gain beam-scanning antenna design is very challenging, taking into account that high radiation efficiency, compact size/volume, and low-cost are key features for mass-market mm-wave applications. In this sense, most of the proposed 5G mobile-antenna solutions are based on phased arrays, which rely on active scanning/beam-forming networks which might be impractical due to an increase cost and manufacturing complexity. However, owning to their characteristics of high-gain, simple-feeding, planar structure, and inherent frequency-beam-scanning behavior, leaky-wave antennas (LWAs) might offer an interesting solution for high-gain low-cost scanning [4].

articleTitle: Experimental Study of a Self-Oscillating Antenna at 5.8 GHz for Breath Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This work presents the application of a 5.8 GHz Self-Injection Locked Oscillator (SILO) for vital signals detection, in particular human breath sensing, without the need of anchor nodes nor remote linked receivers. Specifically, the prototype used for this scope exploits the two cross-polarized fields of an aperture-coupled fed patch antenna that represent the typical input and output ports of a SILO structure. The overall working principle of the system consists in the reception of the frequency-modulated signal coming from the user's chest moving under the effect of breathing. Moreover, this device is fully wearable, i.e. it can be worn by the user under test in the chest position inside a plastic case assuring a suitable distance from the body. Finally, in addition to the respiratory rate, a tentative estimate of the lung capacity is also feasible, with the distinction between normal and deep breath.

articleTitle: A Sum-Difference Pattern Reconfigurable Antenna for Narrow Down Beamwidth of the Subtracted Pattern
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In this paper, a pattern reconfigurable antenna which can be switched between sum and difference (SUM and DIF) beams in E-plane is proposed. Based on the beam switching, a narrow radiation pattern antenna is achieved by subtracting the DIF pattern from the SUM one. With a compact size and simple design, this proposed antenna provides 6.5° narrower beamwidth than that of the SUM beam. It is useful for eliminating unwanted object in short range radar (SRR) applications.

articleTitle: Modeling Propagation Loss in Site-Specific Non-Uniform Dielectric Urban Environments Using VTRPE
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper is continuation of previous work investigating the sensitivity of propagation loss calculations to changes in relative permittivity assigned to features of a sitespecific dense urban landscape. This work adds complexity to the model simulations by introducing non-uniform dielectric definition of the lower boundary condition of the calculation domain. Simulations were done using the Variable Terrain Radiowave Parabolic Equation (VTRPE) model. The geometry of interest is that of a transmitter fixed high above the average building height, with interest in the propagation loss calculated several kilometers down range at receiver heights of a few meters above the ground. The geometry of the lower boundary is defined by urban landscape profiles generated from digital surface models (DSM) derived from vector polygon data. Relative permittivity values for concrete, glass, and brick are assigned with varying arrangements for which simulation results are discussed. Simulation results are shown for 900MHz and 1800MHz for both horizontal and vertical polarizations.

articleTitle: On the Practical Limitations of Electronic Beamsteering using Metamaterials at 28 GHz
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In this paper, the practical limitations and constraints of electronic (active) beamsteering using metamaterials at 28 GHz, in terms of the parasitic elements introduced by varactor diodes, are addressed. Parametric studies will be presented to ascertain the insertion losses of both series inductance and resistance of the varactor diodes used at unit-cell level, in addition to their bandwidth, frequency of resonance and maximum phase shift yielded. This study and characterisation has been performed in simulation environment using CST Microwave Studio.

articleTitle: A Multi Band Planar Inverted-F Antenna with Meandered Slots for Mobile Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In this paper, an Octa-band antenna combining a Planar Inverted-F Antenna (PIFA) and multiple slots on a ground plane for mobile handset applications is presented. The proposed antenna has simple and flat structure that eases the fabrication process. Three slots on the top layer of the antenna substrate are introduced to achieve increased bandwidth and gain characteristics. The proposed structure consists of meander line which makes the antenna to cover the following bands DCS 1800 (1740-1870 MHz), UMTS (1.7-1.87GHz), PCS (1850-1879MHz), Wi-Bro(2.24-2.32GHz), WiMAX (3.50-3.61GHz), Wi-Fi 5GHz (5.21-5.37GHz), WLAN (5.39-5.47GHz) and (7.03-7.93GHz). A stable and omnidirectional radiation patterns are obtained with reasonable gains in the range of 2dB-9dB within different operating bands. Reflection coefficient, VSWR and Radiation patterns are obtained and compared with the values without meander line to show the advantages of multiple bands on PIFA. Ansys HFSS CAD tool has been used for simulations and the results are presented.

articleTitle: Optimization of Elliptical Antenna Arrays Using the Cuckoo Search Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: The main goal of this paper is to study elliptical antenna array (EAA) design and optimization using the cuckoo search (CS) algorithm. The goal of optimization was to minimize the maximum sidelobe level with and without null steering. The CS algorithm is used to determine the excitation amplitudes of the array elements that provide the goal radiation pattern. The effectiveness of the CS in achieving the design goals are illustrated by means of numerical results. Comparisons with other methods are made whenever possible. The considered examples in this paper show the excellent performance and robustness of the CS algorithm and the results reveal that the design of EAAs using the CS algorithm provides considerable enhancements compared with the uniform array and the synthesis obtained using other optimization techniques.

articleTitle: Dual-band UHF RFID tag for metallic items
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This work presents a UHF RFID tag mounted on metallic objects operating in the European and American frequencies (866 and 915 MHz). It is based on a modified patch antenna with a planar structure without the need to shorting pins or holes for a low cost, a very simple and inexpensive manufacturing process with a promising read range of 11m and 9.7m at 866 MHz and 915 MHz respectively.

articleTitle: Performance assessment for OAM antenna arrays
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Towards the short-range multigigabit data transfer, we investigate the possibility of employing the orbital angular momentum (OAM) of electromagnetic (EM) waves in the unlicensed millimeter wave frequency band around 60 GHz (from 57 GHz to 66 GHz). We investigate the effects of OAM source spatial discretization, with respect to the radial and azimuthal coordinates, on a wireless transmission system performance and the quality of OAM radiation patterns. First, second, and third OAM mode are taken into account. Short-range wireless transmission system capabilities are modeled and estimated for realistic values of input parameters. The estimated data transmission rates are very promising.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Patch Antenna With Monopole-Like Radiation Patterns
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In this paper, the TM22 mode of a square patch antenna is excited to generate a monopole-like radiation pattern. The square patch antenna is centrally fed by a coaxial probe, where four shorting pins are rigorously arranged around the feeding point to obtain good impedance match for the antenna. The simulated results demonstrate that the proposed antenna has an impedance bandwidth from 5.73 to 5.91 GHz with a total profile of 0.02λ (λ is the wavelength at 5.8 GHz), the maximal radiation direction is pointing to θ=27o, the gain and radiation patterns within the impedance bandwidth are all about 5.0dBi and monopole-like, respectively. The measured results are consistent with that of simulation.

articleTitle: Design Approach for Modular Millimeter Wave Beamforming Antenna Arrays for 5G Pico-Cells
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In this paper, a concept for a modular 5G beam-forming antenna array is introduced. The array consists of small tiles of planar 2x2 antenna sub-arrays. Each tile contains four patch antennas, a beamformer integrated circuit (BF-IC) and all other components needed to operate the BF-IC in a multilayer package. To build larger beamforming antenna arrays multiple tiles can be combined and placed on a control board. This modular concept leads to highly scalable solutions needed e.g. for various upcoming 5G pico-cell base stations.

articleTitle: A Wideband Crossed-Dipole Antenna for LTE700/GSM850/GSM900 Base Stations
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: A wideband dual-polarized printed folded cross-dipole antenna with a simple structure is proposed for mobile communications at LTE700, GSM850 and GSM900 bands. The antenna is made up of a pair of printed folded dipoles which are perpendicularly crossed together in order to achieve dual polarization. A wideband balun is applied as a feeding structure to each dipole with the purpose of achieving impedance matching over a broad bandwidth. For directional radiation patterns, the dual-polarized printed folded dipole antenna is placed above a shaped reflector. It is verified by experimental measurement that the dual-polarized printed folded antenna can cover a wide frequency band of 6.9-1.0 GHz (37%) for a return loss higher than 15 dB. The isolation is 30 dB. An array that composed of four such dual-polarized antennas has also been fabricated and measured, which achieves a high gain of about 14 dBi with a half-power beamwidth (HPBW) of ~65±8° in the horizontal plane. The proposed broadband dual-polarized folded printed dipole antenna is of value to be used for 3-sector base stations.

articleTitle: Analysis of Influence of Channel Damage on Phased Array Communication Links
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: The phased array communication link is an important form of wireless communication, and the key is to ensure consistency of the amplitude and phase of the phased array radio frequency (RF) channel. Since the RF channel of phased array unit will be damaged due to long working time or lightning stroke, the amplitude and phase of each channel communication signal are inconsistent caused by randomness of the damage, thus resulting in the distortion of synthetic signal and an increase in the bit error rate (BER) of the system. In this paper, the expressions of error vector magnitude (EVM) and BER of phased array communication links after RF channel damage are deduced, and the BER values of communication links under different damage degrees are calculated theoretically. Then, a typical simulation model of phased array communication links is established, and the effects of amplitude and phase inconsistencies on the BER of communication systems are simulated and studied. The results show that when the inconsistency is low (the variance of distribution is small), the degradation degree of communication system is basically consistent with the decrease mean of the amplitude of RF signal. With the increase of the inconsistency of the amplitude and phase, the degradation degree of communication link rises rapidly, far exceeding the change value of signal amplitude.

articleTitle: Helix antenna array based on higher symmetries for antenna miniaturization and mutual coupling reduction
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This document presents the design of an array of helix antennas in axial mode based on higher symmetries. These higher symmetries permit, for a given frequency, the miniaturization of the antenna. Therefore, an array formed by this kind of miniaturized antennas presents lower mutual coupling among the constituting antennas. A comparison is made between the performance of antenna arrays formed by conventional and glide-and-twist-symmetrical helix antennas. The results show a decrease in mutual coupling in the glide-and-twist-symmetrical helix array, regarding to the conventional helix array, for the same element spacing. Moreover, better radiation performance is achieved in terms of directivity and gain in the miniaturized helix array.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Multi-band Circularly Polarized Antenna Using a Back-Lobe Reduction Technique
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper proposes a miniaturized multiband circularly polarized antenna consisting of a folded monopole antenna and an inverted-L antenna on the ground plane. Furthermore, we propose an antenna structure that combines the electric and magnetic current sources to reduce the back-lobe radiation.

articleTitle: Compact Four Element Dual Band Notched Orthogonally Placed UWB Antennas for Wireless MIMO Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: A compact four element dual band notched MIMO antenna catering for UWB applications is proposed. Proposed MIMO antenna is compact having dimensions of 0.45 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.45 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.005 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>. Proposed UWB MIMO antenna system consists of orthogonally placed four antenna elements fed by stepped 50Ω microstrip feedline on 0.508 mm thick GML 1000 substrate. Two split ring resonators (SRR's) are inserted in the radiating element in order to introduce band notches at WLAN-5.2 GHz and X-band-7.5 GHz. Isolation of more than 20 dB is achieved throughout the operating band (3-14 GHz). Radiation patterns, peak gain, radiation efficiency, envelope correlation co-efficient (ECC) and diversity gain of the proposed UWB MIMO antenna are also presented.

articleTitle: Ultra Low Profile Inverted L Antenna Composed of CPW Printed on PET Sheet
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: The ultra low profile inverted L antenna on a rectangular conducting plane is numerically analyzed for the application of IoT. The coplanar waveguide is inserted within the antenna element. The antenna element is printed on the polyethylene terephthalate sheet. The antenna characteristics are discussed.

articleTitle: High Performance Flexible Protocol for Backscattered-Based Neural Implants
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This work presents a custom high-performance protocol for bi-directional communication with neural implants, that will eventually enable closed-loop operation. This protocol presents a flexible configuration to communicate to neural implants with different characteristics. It can support different uplink data rates, a variable number of neural channels from 2 to 16, two types of digital signal modulation (Amplitude Shift-Keying, ASK, and Binary Shift-Keying, PSK), and different RF operation frequencies (915MHz being the default). The proposed protocol is implemented in C++ (preferred to Python because it enables fast signal processing algorithms), using GNU-Radio toolkit with custom communication blocks.

articleTitle: Wideband Spectrum Sensing and Direction Finding Antenna Subsystem
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper presents the design and performance of a wideband amplitude-only direction finding (DF) antenna subsystem. The realized configuration is composed of four two-arm spiral antennas squinted symmetrically off boresight by ±35° to allow a DF capability within a wide field of view (FOV) over 1.58.75GHz frequency range in two orthogonal planes. The four spirals are resistively-terminated and backed by LS2O absorber to maintain good unidirectional operation. All measured spirals have gains of >2dBic, axial ratios <; 3dB over wide FOV, and high quality patterns. The system performance is also estimated and low RMS errors are demonstrated for different incident polarizations.

articleTitle: Disruptive Future of Radar Based on All-Digital PN Signal Processing
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper presents the first results on the design and implementation of a real-time and high resolution monostatic radar at 24 GHz, based on the sliding correlation of pseudonoise (PN) sequences. The real-time radar, with a high time resolution better than 4ns, is used for moving target identification (MTI) in the presence of highly dense clutter, under harsh environments and severe weather conditions (fog, snow and fire smoke or plume). A radar signal processing based on alldigital PN sequences is proposed, which represents a quantum leap in radar future front-end architecture. Results obtained in a controlled environment, inside an anechoic chamber, are presented and a benchmark with a commercially-of-the-shelf solution is presented.

articleTitle: Metantennas: MultiFunctional Metasurface Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Metasurfaces have been widely investigated for antenna design and wave manipulation. As electromagnetic (EM) phenomena are frequency dependent, it is possible to achieve multiple functionalities at the different operating frequencies using a metasurface, namely multifunctional metasurface (MFMS). Based on such a concept of MFMS this paper proposes two shared-aperture metasurface antennas, metantenas for multiband operation. The modal behaviors of metasurface are determined by means of characteristic mode analysis (CMA) for low frequency radiation. As operating frequency increases, the metasurface becomes frequency selective or partially reflection at high frequency bands. The independent modulations of MFMS at each band enable the high flexibility for shared-aperture antenna applications.

articleTitle: MIMO-Sparse Radars for Enhanced DOA Estimation of Spatio-Temporal Correlated Sources
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper investigates an enhanced direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation problem of spatio-temporal correlated sources when a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) sparse radar is deployed. A virtual array with increased degrees-of-freedom (DOF) is realized within two steps by combining MIMO radar with the Khatri-Rao (KR) product approach. Since the final virtual array is a uniform linear array (ULA), a well-known spatial smoothing algorithm is applied to reinforce the rank of its covariance matrix. Meanwhile, the enhanced DOF results in a higher spatial resolution of the radar in the context of DOA estimation.

articleTitle: Vehicle Tracking through Vision-Millimeter Wave Doppler Shift Fusion
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Automated cars benefit greatly from millimeter wave broadband communication links. Also, computer vision is becoming more and more used in automotive applications. In this scenario, we propose a system capable to track the position of a given car on a road by fusing data from a camera system and a wireless radio link at 60 GHz. A Gaussian mixture model and epipolar geometry have been used for computer vision. From a V-band wireless link a Doppler shift estimate has been obtained. The effectiveness of our method is shown on measurement data.

articleTitle: Compact Dual Band F-Shaped ACS-Fed Monopole Antenna for WiMAX and WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: A compact Asymmetric Co-planar Strip (ACS) fed F-shaped monopole antenna catering to 3.5/5.5 GHz WiMAX and 5.8 GHz WLAN applications is proposed. Proposed antenna is electrically small having dimensions of $0.12\,\lambda_{0}\times 0.21 \,\lambda_{0}\,\times\,0.005\,\lambda_{0}$. Compact F-shaped ACS-fed antenna is composed of U-shaped open-ended slot which is tuned properly in order to achieve band notch at 4.5 GHz. By inserting this slot, two frequency passbands are obtained which covers frequency bands for various wireless applications. The frequency bands on which the antenna operates are 3.3 - 3.8 GHz and 5.5 - 6.5 GHz. Simulated and measured results are presented.

articleTitle: Cyclostationary Sources Localization in Wireless Multipath Environment
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: The DOA estimation based on the Cyclic MUSIC, Extended Cyclic MUSIC and their parameterization with the Root-Music approaches is introduced for the communication signals with digital modulation, exhibit the cyclostationary properties. The experimental investigation of the discussed approaches is presented for difficult indoor scenarios include the multipath SOI propagation and powerful in-band interferences.

articleTitle: Co-and Crosspolar Scattering Measurements at Slightly Rough Walls for Indoor Propagation Channels at mmWaves
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper describes a measurement setup to perform channel measurements at 38 GHz based on a standard portable vector network analyzer enhanced by frequency extension modules and appropriate dual mode horn antennas. A measurement campaign for investigation of polarization properties of the indoor channel after single bounce reflection is described and first measurement results are presented.

articleTitle: UWB LPDA Design and Simulations for Jamming
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper summarizes the design and simulated performance of an ultra-wideband (UWB) log-periodic dipole array (LPDA) with typical gain of 7 dBi at frequencies greater than 10:1. This antenna that covers frequency range of 0.425 to 5.9 GHz is basically designed for jamming purposes with a certain power amplifier. The advantage of the LPDA antenna compared to equivalent UWB antennas is light weight and; it can be designed for wider bandwidth.

articleTitle: A Broadband Millimeter Wave Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In this paper a broadband millimeter wave array antenna has been designed at 60-GHz band to be used in millimeter-wave small cell modules. An one dimensional aperture coupled patch antenna has been shown with inverted patch and air gap in between ground and patches. Some unfed patches (dummy patches) are used for performance enhancement. The performance of the antenna is dependent on the air gap, dummy patches and the thickness of the substrates. The air gap has been tuned and the performance has been compared. The antenna shows 55 GHz to 65 GHz bandwidth for /S11/ ∠-10 dB and very flat broadside gain w.r.t. frequency for a single antenna. Peak gain for the single array is obtained 10 dBi. Beamforming with 16 such antennas has been shown to steer the beam ±50 deg at a loss of less than 3 dBi.

articleTitle: Circular Waveguide Array Rectenna Equipped with Pump-Charge and DC-DC Converter Circuits for 1.8GHz RF Energy Harvesting Application
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: One of key performances in radio frequency (RF) energy harvesting application is how to efficiently capture the ambient RF energy to be rectified for energizing small electronic appliances. In this paper, a rectenna equipped with pump-charge and DC-DC converter is proposed for 1.8GHz RF energy harvesting application. The selection of Global System for Mobile communications (GSM) frequency at 1.8GHz is based on the frequent use of these frequencies for communication so that it has potential to receive a lot of RF energy. The proposed rectenna is developed using 2$\times$2 circular waveguide array antenna, while the pump-charge and DC-DC converter circuits are implemented to gain high enough direct current (DC) output voltage from the captured RF signal. The experimental characterization result shows that the RF signal output of circular waveguide array antenna in the range of -10dBm to 1dBm has been successfully rectified to obtain the DC output voltage of 0-2V and 0-3V for pump-charge and DC-DC converter, respectively.

articleTitle: Graph Based Interference Analysis and Resource Allocation in mmWave IoT Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: IoT, Internet of Things is one of the most promising technologies of the fifth-generation (5G). The buzz is all about creating smart environments and getting every type of device connected to the internet. 5G will revolutionize the speed at which the data is transferred, and how much can be transferred at one time. Millimeterwave (mmWave) and massiveMIMO are the two key technologies which plays an essential role to address this problem and represents the next frontier of wireless technology, bringing 10 times higher frequencies and 10 times wider channel bandwidths than the most advanced Wi-Fi and cellular technologies. Millimeter-wave technology is going to become less expensive and easier to deploy, making it a candidate for many wireless connections, including backhaul, personal area networks and LANs. In the world of IoT, this translates into instant, reliable machine communication across every industry and application possible [1]. As the density of wireless devices increases and requirements of all their applications change drastically, it becomes more challenging to provide them connectivity within the stipulated amount of time to deliver the needs. As a result, several challenges such as improving the network capacity, coverage area, efficient data capturing, security, signal processing becomes a necessity to be handled. In line with these, a very recent area of research is to exploit mm-wave band for use in 5G IoT implementations unlike the traditional usage of Zigbee and Bluetooth technologies. One of the technical challenges in this broad area of research is coordinating communication among large number of devices ensuring highly reliable links and investigate on the potential of Resource allocation to envision a diverse set of usage scenarios and applications.

articleTitle: Compact and Wideband Dipole Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Two compact and wideband dipole antennas are proposed in this paper. The first dipole operates at a lowfrequency band from 77.8 MHz to more than 500 MHz with VSWR lower than 2.5:1 and lowest realized gain of -25 dBi at 80 MHz. The second antenna operates at a higher frequency band from 0.5 GHz to more than 6 GHz with VSWR lower than 2.8:1 and a minimum realized gain of -6 dBi at 0.5 GHz. The lowfrequency dipole has a diameter of 0.04 λfmin and a height of 0.13 λfmin, where λfmin is the free-space wavelength at the lowest frequency of operation. While the high-frequency dipole has a diameter of 0.15 λfmin and a height of 0.13 λfmin, where λfmin is the free-space wavelength at the lowest frequency of operation. Both dipoles rely on the monopolar-patch antenna with wideband feed strategy. A curved cone is utilized as the wideband feed. The lowfrequency dipole is fed by a surface-mount RF transformer, which serves as a balun from the coaxial cable to the dipole antenna. The high-frequency dipole is fed by a printed broadband microstrip line to double-sided parallel-strip line transition. These two dipoles are fabricated and measured. The measured VSWR results consistent with the simulated ones for both dipoles.

articleTitle: A Shrinkage L1-Norm Constrained LMS Algorithm for Adaptive Sparse Array Beamforming
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: A constrained least-mean-square (CLMS) algorithm using shrinkage method and l<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>-norm penalty, namely, the shrinkage l<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>-norm penalized CLMS (SL<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>-CLMS) algorithm is proposed for adaptive beamforming. The introduced algorithm can successfully exploit the sparse characteristics of the antenna array utilized in beamformer. Besides, the new algorithm maintains the desired performance, i.e., greeting main lobe and nulls corresponding to the signal of interest (SO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>) and interferences. The SL<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>-CLMS algorithm employs an alterable step step which is acquired through the l<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>-l<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> minimization method to accelerate the convergence rate. Simulation results attest the validity of the SL<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>-CLMS algorithm.

articleTitle: Electronically Beam-steerable Dual-band Reflectarray for Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel continuously beam-steering dual-band, dual circularly polarized (CP) reflectarray. The dual band operation of the reflectarray is obtained by using the interleaved circularly polarized triangular patches as the radiating elements. Each of the patches has two proximity feed lines that are electromagnetically coupled to a branch line coupler, where the phase shifters are integrated. The phase shifter is realized by using a new type of high-frequency tunable dielectric materials, Lead Niobate Pyrochlores Pb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub> Nb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5+n</sub> (PN). By controlling the applied voltage, the dielectric permittivity of the PN material can be changed. This characteristic is utilized to the design of tunable dielectric capacitors, which is placed between the ground and the signal line of a Co-planar waveguide (CPW) transmission line. To validate the design concept, X-band passive antenna prototype was designed, fabricated and measured. Preliminary results on the designed phase shifter and tunable dielectric materials are also presented in this paper.

articleTitle: MercuryDPM Adaptation for Electromagnetic Microscopic DEM Simulation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: The purpose of this research is to create the adapted software for modeling microscopic electrodynamics processes. We use open source product codes MercuryDPM [1]. The basis of mathematical calculations and event processing is carried out by the method of discrete particles [2]. In the process of adapting the code, a number of fundamental models are considered: electron in a vacuum at rest, the electron moves in a vacuum as a non-relativistic particle and as a relativistic particle, the electron moves in the medium (gas, liquid, solid). The main types of interaction: electron - electron, electron - atom, electron - surface. This study is a synthesis of known processes into a single program. The project is limited in scope to the observed effects - it does not affect quantum effects (such as quantum particle scattering). The upper limit is macroeffects - such concepts of generalization as electric current, dielectric and magnetic permeability are excluded from the project. In this paper, we follow the general concept outlined in [3], but in the context of electrodynamics. The main output characteristic of the solver is the electromagnetic field emitted by the electron. We use the strict formulation [3].

articleTitle: Wide Bandwidth Dual Port, Dual Sense Circular Polarization Antenna for Satellite Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper presents a large bandwidth dual-sense-of circular polarization (CP) patch antenna working at X-band. The radiating element is suspended in air by three pins that are sequentially-fed to provide robust CP. The antenna feed network can switch from left-handed CP (LHCP) to right-handed CP (RHCP) on the base on the connected port and, being compact, can be placed at the back of the antenna ground plane. Furthermore, to minimize the cross-polarization at low elevation angles, the so called “monopole fence”, positioned around the metallic patch element, was proposed and designed to improve cross-polarization and to reduce the on axis gain for a wide beam-width.

articleTitle: Diversity Antenna for Vehicular Communications in Microwave and mm-Wave Bands
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: A dual band diversity antenna is proposed for vehicular communications. The antenna works at both 5.9 GHz and 60 GHz simultaneously which makes it a suitable candidate for next generation intelligent transportation systems (ITS). High isolation of the two antenna elements with transmission less than -25 dB at both bands guarantees an optimum diversity performance. The theoretical limit of the diversity gain according to the propagation condition is investigated. It is shown that the effective diversity antenna gain (DAG) of the design is 8.7 dB in a uniform propagation scenario which is only 0.04 dB less than the theoretical limit.

articleTitle: Spiral Antenna With a Circular HIS Reflector
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper describes the antenna characteristics of a spiral antenna with a circular high-impedance surface (HIS) reflector (CirHISR). The CirHISR consists of a fan-shaped patch element array printed on the top surface of a circular dielectric substrate, and a perfect electric conducting reflector printed on the bottom surface of the circular dielectric substrate. The aspect ratio of each fan-shaped patch element, which is defined by the ratio of patch width to patch length, is approximately one. The axial ratio characteristics are analyzed using FEKO software based on the Method of Moment. Good axial ratio is obtained across a frequency range of 3 GHz to 10 GHz, where the antenna height is 0.9 cm (0.09 wavelengh at the lowest analysis frequency). In addition, other antenna characteristics, including VSWR, gain, and radiation efficiency are recognized.

articleTitle: Design of a six-patch series-fed traveling-wave antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Leaky wave antennas are well-known for narrow-beam antennas with a frequency dependent antenna pattern which could be used for beamsteering radar or telecommunication applications. In this paper we shortly present an easy-to-implement approach for a traveling wave antenna on microstrip technology which is more broadband than a classical resonant antenna and thus less sensitive to process tolerances. Both kind of antennas, the traveling wave and the resonant antenna, are manufactured and measured. The simulation and measurement result of both antennas are compared to each other and discussed.

articleTitle: Cost-Effective Testbed for Cognitive Long-Range Communications based on Antenna Array and Software Defined Radio
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Main objective of this work is to design and implement a cost-effective testbed for cognitive long-range communication system based on a high gain planar antenna array and Software Defined Radio (SDR) kits. Antenna integration, miniaturization and feeding network optimization have been properly executed for designing a 4x4 linear antenna array in order to achieve a return loss of -25 dB and a directivity of 19.04 dB at 2.4 GHz with a bandwidth of 18.5 MHz. Primary cognitive communication link has been established based on a Frequency Hoping (FH) scheme in the transmitter and receiver sides integrated with an energy detection spectrum sensing block, which enables the receiver seeking the operating frequency of the transmitter and synchronizing with it. Finally, a real-world testbed has been implemented using SDR units to transmit and receive text messages properly. This designed testbed can achieve a Point to Point (P2P) link of about 20 Km based on a cheap SDR with a sensitivity of -75 dBm and a 10 dBm transmitting power.

articleTitle: SLM 3D-Printed Active Phased Array for X-Band Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: The development of an X-band active antenna array using selective laser melting (SLM) additive manufacturing. The array consists of Vivaldi antenna elements integrated with a low noise amplifier (LNA) close to the feed. When integrated with the antenna array the LNA achieves a noise figure of less than 1. 3 dB over the frequency band.

articleTitle: Tilted Beam from a Spiral Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: The two arms of a spiral antenna are made of metalines. This spiral antenna is designed for steering its circularly polarized (CP) beam in the vertical plane. For this, two factors are introduced for the antenna excitation: phase factor ξ and voltage factor Ω The excitation is decomposed into balanced and unbalanced excitation terms. The balanced term generates a broadside beam, called the B-beam, which is transformed into a tilted beam by the unbalanced term generating a beam off the broadside axis, called the U-beam. It is found that, when the phase factor is fixed to be ξ = 0, the tilted beam seamlessly scans in the vertical plane with change in voltage factor Ω.

articleTitle: High Gain Beam Steerable Phased Array Incorporating Reconfigurable Parasitics formed from Liquid Metal
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper presents a beam switchable antenna for use as the radiating element within a phased array and shows how it can be used to increase the scan angle range of a phased array. The radiating element consists of a driven dipole and a series of directors. A group of 3 directors are aligned along each of the 2 beam switching directions. The directors are formed from liquid metal. By moving the liquid metal from one set of directors to the other it is possible to switch the beam direction between ± 25<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup>. The novel radiating element is used within a phase array. By employing a combination of beam switching at the element factor level and beam steering at the array factor level we are able to obtain an ±9<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup> (i.e. 18<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup> total) increase in the scan angle range at the expense of a slight reduction in the realized gain.

articleTitle: Implementation of Dynamic Directional Modulation with Software Defined Radio
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Dynamic Directional Modulation (DDM) is a technique for phased arrays that can increase security in the physical layer. In this work, we present a setup for a DDM system where the array feeding network is fully implemented with Software Defined Radio (SDR). The calibration of the system is discussed, and some experiments are carried out to demonstrate the tradeoff between security and transmitted power.

articleTitle: Design of an UHF POD Antenna and Its Efficiency Optimization by Genetic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This work presents a process of designing a Printed-On-Display (POD) antenna which is optically transparent, based on the ITO (Indium-Tin-Oxide) material. For searching for highest efficiency of POD antenna, the Genetic Algorithms (GA) is applied as an optimization tool. After the GA process, the resultant simulated antenna model is realized on the glass. A POD antenna for receiving DVB-T digital TV signal (UHF band) is realized and demonstrated.

articleTitle: Leaky-Wave Antennas with Loaded Complementary Components for High-Performance and Wideband Application
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Complementary structures are widely used in antenna design to achieve excellent performance. In this paper, our recent efforts in deploying complementary components in designing leaky-wave antennas (LWAs) with high performance are reviewed with emphasis on (1) suppression of open-stopband aiming to broadside radiation, (2) gain and radiation efficiency stabilization over the entire operation band of an LWA, and (3) suppression of frequency beam scanning of an LWA. Our design methods are effective to improve LWAs and extend their application scenarios.

articleTitle: Energy Resources Management Enabled by Internet of Things Devices
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: The participation of small end-users in the smart grid brings benefits for the end-users and for the smart grid. This paper will treat end-users using communities involving energy sharing between private buildings (residential and commercial) and public buildings. The energy can be shared among end-users and the community can be managed centralized. The paper uses IoT devices to enable the active participation of end-users. The use of this type of devices is growing and more and more market available product are appearing. The remote control and monitor capabilities, provided by the normality of IoT devices, can and should be used in energy management systems as enablers. This paper uses IoT devices, located in end-users, to enable the participation of these player in the community. The paper will propose a smart energy community platform and show its results.

Author Keywords: IoT devices for demand side management

articleTitle: Monocone Antenna with Inverted -L and -F Structure
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: The monocone antenna is a type of monopole antenna and has wideband characteristics. In this paper, a low-profile monocone antenna by using planar inverted-F structure is proposed. The characteristics of the proposed antenna are analyzed by simulation. As a result, the low-profile antenna can be obtained while the wideband is maintained. Relative bandwidth of VSWR $\le$ 2 is more than 166.3%. In addition, miniaturization of the monocone antenna can be found.

articleTitle: 2.4 GHz RF Propagation Measurements and Modeling in A Paddy Field for A Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper describes 2.4 GHz RF peer-to-peer propagation measurements and modeling in a Japonica paddy field during 5 stages of the growth season: transplantation, panicle initiation, booting, flowering, and grain filling. From the perspective of practicality for the various setting conditions of a sensor unit, the antenna heights were placed 55,105 and 155 cm from the ground in order to evaluate signal propagation through vegetation. Detailed measurement curves of RSSI (received signal strength indication) against distance indicate the presence of various vegetation types based on the moisture conditions of plant growth. The SRET (simplified radiative energy transfer)-based model fits well depending on leaf density for NLOS (non-line-of-sight) conditions. In the case of LOS (line-of-sight) conditions, a novel model named the “TRPF (two-ray paddy field) model” is proposed in order to express the influence of vegetation for a reflection wave.

articleTitle: A comparative study of the harvested wireless power using multiple antenna designs implemented in a common domestic environment
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study over a relationship between the extent of the received voltage and received power by three diverse antennas. The antennas were designed for two distinct frequency bands and fabricated using the conventional etching techniques as well as the modern inkjet printing techniques. Three antennas namely, etched slot antenna, Ultra Wide Band antenna and inkjet-printed slot antenna were designed and created using the conventional etching techniques as well as the modern inkjet printing techniques. The three antennas worked well at the designed frequency with a good correlation established between the simulated and the measured results.

articleTitle: Microwave Encoders and Application to Near-Field Chipless-RFID: a Review
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Recently, electromagnetic encoders operating at microwave frequencies have been reported. Such encoders can be useful for measuring linear and angular displacements and velocities, but also as near-field chipless-RFID tags. In both cases, encoder reading is carried out by proximity, through near field, by using a microwave interrogation signal. This paper reports the recent advances relative to such microwave encoders, with special emphasis on chipless-RFID applications. Two types of encoders are considered: (i) those with printed metallic elements on a dielectric substrate, and (ii) full dielectric encoders, where the metallic elements are replaced with dielectric inclusions.

articleTitle: Realization of circularly polarized antenna array with parasitic patches
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper presents results of practical realization of a circularly polarized patch antenna array fitted with parasitic patches to increase axial ratio bandwidth. Measurements show good match with the simulations. Manufacturing specifics are discussed.

articleTitle: On the Matching of Stripline-Fed Cavity-Backed Slots as a Series-Fed Array Element
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Two ways of increasing the working bandwidth of series-fed Cavity-Backed Slots (CBS) are presented and analysed in this contribution. One of them consists in increasing the off-set feeding distance of the slot. The other one adds a matching stub in the feeding line. Simulation results of both ways for matching the same slot are provided. Results show that the matching stub can be used along a wider bandwidth effectively, but, in this case, an asymmetric stripline or enclosed microstrip are the only option to feed the CBS.

articleTitle: On The Outage Performance Of Line-Of-Sight Massive MIMO with a Fixed-Length Uniform Linear Sparse Array
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Increasing the inter-element spacing of a uniform linear sparse array results in reducing the mutual coupling and simplifying the heat dissipation control of the array. However, increasing the inter-element spacing may result in the appearance of grating lobes in the field-of-view (FoV). In this paper, 0.05-outage capacity is used as the performance metric to optimize the inter-element spacing for a given array size in line-of-sight scenarios. For the case of two users, we propose to increase the inter-element spacing as long as the 0.05-outage capacity does not reduce more than 1% compared to the capacity achieved when the two users have orthogonal channel vectors. Radiated power at the base station is adjusted to have the same effective isotropic radiated power for different arrays. Simulation results for an array size of 40λ show that for FoVs of 60° to 120°, the inter-element spacing can be increased from 0.5λ to more than 1.14λ.

articleTitle: A Broadband Full-Wave Dipole Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This work presents a broadband four-element antenna array using full-wave dipole (FWD). The broad impedance bandwidth is realized by introducing gaps in both two arms of the dipole. Besides, the proposed antenna element can achieve a higher gain than hall-wave dipole (HWD) antennas due to the electrically large size of the FWD. The impedance bandwidth and 3-dB gain bandwidth of proposed antenna array is 67.8% and 51.4%, respectively. The proposed methodology is good for high gain antenna array design because it reduces the number of antenna elements and the complexity of power distributed network by using the high gain FWD.

articleTitle: Analysis and Measurement of Diode Mounting Meta-surface for Reflection Beam Control
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: We proposed to adopt meta-surface to improve the propagation environment of IoT (Internet of Things). Metasurface set close to IoT terminal can be changing the reflection direction of radio waves. It is also possible to switch the beam direction using diodes attached to each patch of meta-surface. However, the circuit design to control the ON and OFF the voltage of the diode on this meta-surface, the study on the influence of this bias circuit on the radiation characteristics of the meta-surface is insufficient, and the diode-mounted metasurface Evaluation by measurement of was not carried out. To address the issues, we design the bias circuit for the diode mounted meta-surface that can switch the beam direction by changing on and off this diode and achieved the method to avoid the undesired radiation from the feed line of bias circuit.

articleTitle: N-dimensional M-ary Constant Energy Modulation for Nonlinear Communications Channels
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In this paper, we present a multidimensional constant energy modulation, which utilizes N-dimensional signal space to provide a very large set of M-ary signal constellations. The modulation is termed as (ND-MCEM). This modulation provides good spectral efficiency while constraining all possible communications symbols to a constant energy with the goal of improving performance over nonlinear communications channels.

articleTitle: The Distributed Resource Allocation for D2D Communication with Game Theory
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a distributed resource allocation algorithm based on game theory to solve the problem of cross-tier interference between device-to-device (D2D) communication and cellular users and the co-tier interference between D2D communication. We assume that the D2D user is forced to reuse the channel resources of multiple cellular users, while the resources of each cellular user can be reused by multiple D2D users. Moreover, the resource allocation problem between cellular users and D2D users is modeled as a non-cooperative game, and each participant is selfish and wants to maximize its utility. At the same time, D2D users coordinate the co-tier interference in a cooperative manner. The simulation results show that the proposed distributed algorithm has a significant improvement in term of throughput with guaranteeing the quality of service (QoS) requirement when compared with the existing algorithms.

articleTitle: Implementation of 5G beamforming techniques on cylindrical arrays
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In this paper we study the performance of a Uniform Cylindrical Array for a 5G base station working in the mmW region. Conventional and Capon beamforming design are considered. A comparison against a base station equipped with three Uniform Planar Arrays, one per sector, is presented. Average per-user achievable rate results are provided with different system configuration in terms of network loading and number of antennas, showing that Uniform Cylindrical Array could represent an interesting solution for 5GmmW networks.

articleTitle: Wideband Circularly Polarized 3D Wire Antenna for Wi-MAX Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In this paper, a crooked wire antenna is optimized to be functional in both the WLAN and the Wi-Max bands (2.4-2.48 and 3.3-3.7 GHz). The antenna presents a right-hand circular polarization (RHCP) with a 3 dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of 3.28 to 4.11 GHz. For the WLAN band (2.4-2.48 GHz), the polarization was linear. The antenna is fabricated using 3D printing techniques and occupy a total volume of 33.8 mm × 30.4 mm × 37.4 mm. The simulated and measured farfield results show good agreement with a radiation pattern that assures a near hemispherical coverage toward the upper hemisphere and a measured maximum gain value of approximately 6 dB. The radiation pattern of the antenna assures a near hemispherical coverage toward the upper hemisphere.

articleTitle: New Architecture for Wireless 230V Powered Products Based on Isolated Microstrip Line
