publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper presents a new architecture for products powered by the mains and having an external RF connector where isolation is done on the RF transmission line, removing the bulky and expensive isolation transformer commonly used at power supply stage. To achieve it, Y2 safety capacitors are associated to the microstrip transmission line. Transmission losses at 868 MHz are measured at 1.34 dB with 3 capacitors in series to achieve an insulation level of 6 kV.

articleTitle: A Block-sparse Set-Membership PNLMS Algorithm Based on Hybrid Zero-Attraction Penalty
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In some practical communication systems, the channel impulse responses whose values are large but just account for a small fraction distributed in clusters. Hybrid norm l<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2,</sub><sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is employed as a zero-attraction penalty to build the cost function (CF) of the proportional normalized least mean square (PNLMS) algorithm. In addition, the set-membership (SM) criterion is also used to reduce the computing complexity and to get good tracking performance by presetting a thresh-old of error. The novel method named l<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2,</sub><sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>-set-membership PNLMS (l<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2,</sub><sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>-SMPNLMS) algorithm not only has fast initial convergence speed inheriting from the PNLMS algorithm, but also has good performance to deal with block-sparse signals. Numerical simulations have been conducted and the result shows the superiority of the proposed algorithm compared with the related algorithms.

articleTitle: OFDM Channel Sounding in Line - of - Sight V2V Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Traditionally, the empirical characterization of (mobile or not) radio channels has been requiring the use of bulky, costly and power demanding Channel Sounders (CS). Even though the channel can be characterized with a high degree of accuracy, these instruments may be difficult to deploy in some situations. For example, in the fast characterization of Vehicle - to - Vehicle (V2V) channels, the size of the sounding system may be an issue. In this communication, we present a CS based on the Orthogonal Frequency-Division Multiplexing (OFDM) in the 5.9 GHz band. As we will show, the hardware implementation, which is based on Software Defined Radios (SDR), makes possible to save energy and cost as long as providing embeddability.

articleTitle: Miniaturized MACKEY Type S Providing a Short Circuit Plate at the End
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: A meta-surface inspired antenna (MACKEY) has been proposed, which works not only in free space but also on a metal plate. In this paper, MACKEY Type S miniaturized by providing a short circuit plate at the end will be shown.

articleTitle: Slant Polarised Crossed Bow-tie Antenna Array with Reduced Number of Phase Shifters and an Embedded Feed Network
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper presents a two-element dual slant polarized crossed bow-tie phased array antenna with an integrated feed network to decrease the overall number of phase shifters and ports. The dual polarised antenna is composed of two perpendicular bow-tie antennas. In the proposed groundless feeding structure each half of the crossed bow-tie antenna shares its feeding network with the half of the neighbouring crossed bowtie element to reduce the number of phase shifters and excitation ports by 50%. The structure is designed to operate at 4.5 GHz centre frequency with 400 MHz bandwidth and 9.21 dBi realized gain.

articleTitle: Sommerfeld half-space and path loss improvement in near-ground wave propagation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper is a communication about the near-ground propagation and the condition under which the proximity of a lossy interface improves the path loss [1]. The well-known Sommerfeld half-space problem is treated by Sommerfeld formulation which is widely accepted in the community and can be validated by rigorous mathematical treatment [2]. The asymptotic approximation (steepest descent) of the electric field radiated by an elementary vertical electric dipole (VED) over a half-space is of interest. It is important to note that the formulation includes not only the direct and reflected waves, but also a third field component generated thanks to diffraction at the interface between the two media. This third component is naturally ignored by ray based techniques and in some cases can become predominant and improves the near-ground path loss. The appropriately simplified field expression brings out the important intervening parameters, such as the working frequency, the heights of the elementary dipoles and the interface's electrical properties (permittivity and conductivity). In this paper, the condition for the optimal near-ground path loss is presented explicitly as a function of these three parameters. More information about the optimised path loss zone can be extracted using two distances. The first distance (ρ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">min</sub>) is calculated to estimate the shortest possible distance to achieve the optimised path loss. The second distance (ρ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">break</sub>) is calculated to predict the end of the advantageous zone. These three easy-to-use expressions (Figure 1.a) help to take full advantage of the near-ground link and will be presented and discussed in the final submission.

articleTitle: Antenna Modeling by Near Field Equivalent Sources in Radio Frequency Interoperability
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper deals with the use of Electro Magnetic (EM) simulation in Radio Frequency Interoperability (RFI) problems [1]. More specifically, the feasibility of antenna modeling with near field equivalent sources in Ultra High Frequency (UHF) band is presented. After a brief introduction, section II describes RFI context and the methodology used to treat RFI problems on large platforms. A focus on the benefit brought by Electro Magnetic (EM) simulation is done, underlying the key point of antenna modeling in EM simulation representativeness. In section III, antenna modeling by near-field equivalent sources derived from measurement is introduced and validated on two applications cases in UHF band. The first one is the calculation of installed radiating performance, and the second one is the calculation of antennas coupling coefficient. Finally, conclusions are drawn.

articleTitle: Evaluation Method of Resonant Coils to Obtain Diameter-to-Diameter Transmission Distance of Resonant Coil
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In this paper, the design method is presented through the equivalent circuit analysis of resonator to obtain the diameter-to-diameter transmission distance.

articleTitle: A Study on the Mutual Coupling Effects of the Ultra-Wideband Vivaldi Array
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper presents a detailed Study on the mutual coupling of the ultra-wideband vivaldi array from 1GHz to 9GHz through the simulation and displays the distribution of the coupling at different frequencies. The active VSWRs of the elements towards to different steering angles are then calculated from S-Matrix of the finite array by summing all the coupled energies surrounding the element, which shows that the active VSWRs of some elements in frequency below 3GHz are much bigger than in frequency above 3GHz. However, the total mismatch loss at the lower band is no more than 2.1dB even though active VSWRs of some elements go up sharply. Finally, the effect of adding passive elements surrounding the array to reduce the edge effects is evaluated by comparing the total mismatch losses, which indicates that it may not lead to improvement of the performance from view of matching.

articleTitle: TEM Horn Inspired Wideband Antennas for Diverse Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Two implementations of transverse electromagnetic (TEM) horns are researched for wideband receiving (RX) and transmitting (TX) applications. Both configurations are flush-mountable and inspired by a combined TEM horn/loop design. For RX application, a 46:1 bandwidth antenna recessed in an absorptive cavity is developed having in mind requirements of an amplitude-only direction finding antenna subsystem. For TX operation, an integration approach is proposed to assimilate the antenna with a lossless cavity and eliminate excitation of cavity modes that may degrade its performance. This is enabled by the realization of a compact, high-power, and flush-mountable TEM horn array. Theory and experiments validate designs robustness and show good performance in both cases.

articleTitle: Statistical study of the matching properties of high density randomly distributed dipoles
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: UHF RFID (Radio Frequency IDentification) technologies have a long established role for tracking and identification of objects and persons. In some applications the density of RFID tags is high, this can give rise to an important electromagnetic coupling between tag antennas which modifies antenna's key parameters, i.e., matching properties and radiation pattern. These electromagnetic modifications can alter the communication links between devices and thus degrade the read rate or the read range of an RFID system. The mutual coupling between RFID tags has been investigated in literature [1], however the statistical modelling of the impact of the mutual coupling for high densities of RFID tags is still a new topic [2].

articleTitle: Low-profile Half Wavelength Ultra Wide Band Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In this paper, the newly proposed designed antenna with low profile has overcome physical problems of the existing antenna for the aircraft or vehicles, and have performance suitable for wideband characteristics. The proposed antenna was designed with a half-wavelength hemispherical structure by applying the self-complementary principle and image theory. The size of antenna is 400 mm(diameter) × 200 mm(height). As a result, and the radiation patterns are similar to monopole antenna. Next, the structure of a redesigned rectangular a half-wavelength loop antenna for easy of fabrication. This antenna has a size of 196 mm(width) × 156.3 mm(height) × 158.7 mm(length). The radiation patterns are similar to the monopole antenna of a half-wavelength hemispherical structure. Finally, we newly proposed a low-profile wideband antenna to ensure a low-profile structure, while retaining the wideband characteristics. The low-profile wideband antenna has a size of 315 mm (width) × 110 mm(height) × 295 mm(length). The radiation patterns of the antenna are similar to those described earlier. Therefore, it is a new type of low profile and ultra wide band(100:1) antenna suitable for mounting the aircraft or vehicles.

articleTitle: Novel Dual Band and Ultra-Wide Band Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: The frequency bands used by modern communication devices occupied substantial portion of the spectrum opened to public. In addition to the licensed bands that belong to wireless service providers, all communication devices use unlicensed portions of the spectrum. The differences between the operation frequencies are very big, consequently usually there are several separate or tunable antennas in communication devices. The 5th generation wireless systems (5G) and Internet-of-Things with new operation frequency bands, carrier aggregations and enhanced spectral efficiency impose new challenges on antenna designs.

articleTitle: Novel Inkjet-Printed Chipless Tags for Radio-Frequency-Identification Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In radio-frequency-identification (RFID) systems, chipless tags, i.e., tags without microchips, are desirable in comparison to their more common counterparts involving microchips. This is not merely due to the extra costs of microchips but also due to relatively difficult mounting processes to attach microchips onto metallic antennas, which in fact becomes challenging if tags are produced via inkjet printing methods. In the context of paper-based inkjet printing, absence of microchips is also attractive for green technology, since tags that contain only paper and metallic prints may be easier to recycle. On the other hand, the resulting RFID systems need to operate in a range of frequencies (rather than operating at a single frequency) in order to encode bits based on frequency-dependent responses of tag structures. In addition, one must consider potential difficulties in accurate and reliable identification, especially due to typically low signal levels. These difficulties, together with other constraints, such as compactness and being easy to fabricate, make it an essential task to design suitable tag geometries for chipless RFID systems.

articleTitle: Comparative Performance Analysis of Training Sequences in Equalization
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: During the last decade we have experienced an increasing demand for wireless communication systems, that require the implementation of different functions, including equalization, to establish a reliable connection between nodes of the network. The correlation and statistical properties of the training sequences have been exploited in wireless systems in the past, however there are few studies that compare the impact of these sequences on the efficacy of the equalization process where they are implemented. Our experimental design considers five well known training sequences of the same length, including Barker, Willard, Neuman-Huffman, a Random binary sequence, and the Zadoff-Chu (ZC) code, and a new proposed sequence. The simulation results show that Random code is the best performing training sequence, especially when it is used in environments with strong levels of inter-symbol interference (ISI), ZC performs better for conditions with lower ISI and our proposed sequence named EoP performs in second place for any ISI level.

articleTitle: Analysis of S-band Microwave Propagation in a Closed Metal Chamber
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In this work, signal propagation problem inside a metal structure is studied to explore the possibility of replacing the communication cables of aircrafts by wireless technology. To study this problem, a 3-dimension structure is modeled and simulated using full-wave method. The major difficulties are strong standing wave and small apertures which has a cutoff frequency higher than the employed spectrum. This problem is solved when the aperture is enlarged enough.

articleTitle: Diffuse terrestrial scatter contributions to multi-hop skywave propagation in OTH radar systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Rising interest in exploiting multi-hop skywave propagation for OTH radar surveillance and remote sensing at extreme ranges has drawn attention to the need for a more accurate model of the channel transfer function. In particular, diffuse scattering in the intermediate ground reflection zones has long been identified as a potential contributor to path loss, group range spread, Doppler modulation and polarisation filtering [1], but present-day models employed in operational OTH radar systems rely almost exclusively on crude scalar corrections to account for reflection loss, ignoring other effects.

articleTitle: Frequency-Scanned Active Monopulse Radar based on Bluetooth Low Energy Devices using an Array of Two Planar Leaky-Wave Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: A novel technique for angular location of mobile devices, with a wide field of view (FoV) and low cost is presented in this work. The technique is based on the use of the three Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) advertising channels, which are located at the frequencies 2.402 GHz, 2.426 GHz and 2.48 GHz, and the received power information included in the RSSI field of the BLE packets. With the use of an array of two planar and passive leaky-wave antennas (LWA), with two ports each (a total of four ports), due to their inherent frequency scanning, 12 directive beams can be synthesized (one for each frequency channel and port of the array), with different pointing angles and overlapping to obtain different monopulse functions combining information from each port and channel, which complement each other to cover a FoV in the wide angular range [-60°, +60°]. Analog and digital measurements are presented to show the viability and limitations of the technique.

articleTitle: Design of a New Type Phase Shifting Array with Dual Radiating Modes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach that integrates the radiating behaviors of reflectarrays and transmitarrays together. A new type dual-mode phase shifting array is applied for validation, which consists of split-diagonal-cross unit cells and a polarizing grid. The horizontal and vertical polarized incident waves are separated into reflecting and transmitting modes due to the grid. Accordingly, one can easily switch the array between the forward and backward radiating modes individually. This simple solution could be potential as the increasing requirement of high integration in modern communications.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Wireless Power Transfer System for Prosthetic Hands
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In this paper, a wireless power transfer (WPT) system is proposed to supply power continuously to a prosthetic hand. The transmitter circuit (class-E power amplifier) and WPT coils are modeled and implemented along with commercially available receiver circuit and multiple motors. Tissue safety to thermal load is simulated by measuring the tissue specific absorption rate (SAR) using the commercial electromagnetic simulator ANSYS HFSS. The calculated and simulated results of the designed WPT system is validated by measuring the received power where the TX coil mounted on an artificial wrist part is filled with phantom mimicking the properties of human muscle. An algorithm is also proposed to monitor and control the rotation of the prosthetic hand utilizing wireless power.

articleTitle: SSPE Method Including Backward Term for an EM Propagation Real Case Study
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper presents the addition of the Backward term in a Split Step Parabolic Equation (SSPE) algorithm to estimate radiofrequency coverage in a realistic and lossy terrain. In order to evaluate the accuracy of the PE model, results of measurement campaigns and Method of Moments (MoM) were used. This article has preliminary results that will motivate tests in higher frequencies where the presence of Backward Term can be more appreciated.

articleTitle: Practical Performance of Regular Sparse Array Direction of Arrival Estimation in 1-D
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Recently, a new algorithm for robust direction of arrival (DoA) estimation, using regular sparse array antenna systems, was described in [1]. Aliasing (grating lobes) is removed through the use of two sparse arrays - one a shifted version of the other. Minimum spacing between any two elements is not required to be smaller than a half wavelength. The method completely removes the dense Nyquist spacing requirement, allowing improved resolution for a fixed number of sensors and reduced mutual coupling between antenna elements. Because of a shared structured linear system of equations between the two arrays, as a consequence of the shift between the two, the analysis of both is automatically paired, thereby avoiding a computationally expensive matching step as is required in the use of so-called coprime arrays. Furthermore, the method provides an accurate estimate of the number of signals impinging on the system without any prior knowledge, while there is no requirement that the respective signals be uncorrelated. Distinct, fully coherent signals, such as those that occur in a multipath environment, can thus be accurately distinguished. Several examples were presented in [1], investigating both the performance in increasing noise, as well as increasing mutual coupling scenarios. In all of these, the new method performs better than standard techniques on a variety of metrics.

articleTitle: APWC 2019 Plenary Lectures
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Provides an abstract for each of the plenary presentations and may include a brief professional biography of each presenter. The complete presentations were not made available for publication as part of the conference proceedings.

articleTitle: A Compact Circularly Polarized High-Gain Antenna Array for Ka-Band CubeSats Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In this work, we present a high-gain, low-profile circularly polarized 8×8 element antenna array operating in Ka-band at 35 GHz. The antenna is a great fit for establishing a communication link between a CubeSat and ground station. The performance was validated using full-wave simulation. Finally, a prototype of the antenna was manufactured by 3D-printing and its performance was measured.

articleTitle: An Unbalanced-Feed Grid Array Antenna Composed of Diamond-Shaped Elements Printed on a Dielectric Substrate
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: An unbalanced-feed grid array antenna composed of diamond-shaped elements printed on a dielectric substrate (UB-Dia-PGAA) is analyzed using the method of moments. It is found that the directivity for the UB-Dia-PGAA is higher than that for a conventional unbalanced-feed printed grid array antenna. It follows that the bend angle of the diamond-shaped element contributes to increasing the directivity for the UB-Dia-PGAA.

articleTitle: A Novel Antenna Covered by Planar Inverted-L Stub to Keep the Communication Distance whether Optional Circuit Board Exist or not
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In a recent couple of years, the smart meter system is installed at each home, factory and company. The smart meter system has Route A and B for data collection and visualization of power consumption. Route A is indispensable, Route B is option function. In this study, we present a novel antenna to keep the communication distance whether Route B option circuit board exist or not. A distinctive feature of the proposed antenna structure is a planar inverted-L stub between a monopole antenna and option circuit board. This planar inverted-L stub archives reduction of the electric coupling between the monopole antenna and option circuit board. The total efficiency of the proposed antenna improves 22 dB compared with conventional monopole antenna. This paper provides design guideline and some key parameters of the proposed antenna.

articleTitle: Optimal Antenna Array Topologies for Energy Efficiency Maximization by Employing Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: The purpose of this work is to design novel antenna array topologies that maximize the energy efficiency (EE) in multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) wireless systems. To provide insights into EE optimization issues, the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm is employed as an effective technique. First, we adopt a flexible and generalized three-dimensional (3D) angle of arrival (AOA) model to account for realistic propagation environments. Then we derive a novel closed-form spatial correlation function (SCF) relevant to the locations of antenna array elements in the 3D space. In this paper, we incorporate our SCF into the EE derivation and apply the PSO algorithm to find the optimal antenna array topology in space that maximizes the EE. The derived EE is significantly higher compared to existing state-of-the art research that employed an exponential SCF. We provide new insights into EE maximization for antenna arrays, where the simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness and usefulness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Recovery Performance of LpLq-ADMM Algorithm under SαS impulse Noise
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In the process of signal and image acquisition and transmission, there is not only the additive white Gaussian noise interference, but also the non-Gaussian noise interference. The performance of a standard reconstruction algorithm, known as compressed sensing, can be significantly reduced if it is used to recover the signal affected by non-Gaussian noise. In this paper, LpLq-ADMM algorithm (p ∈ ( 0, 2 ) , q ∈ ( 0, 1 )) based on alternating direction method of multipliers is proposed to improve the reconstruction accuracy and the robustness of signal and image restoration in impulsive SαS (symmetric α-stable) noise. Lp-norm is used as the loss function term to enhance the data restoration ability in SαS noise and Lq-norm is used as the generalized non-convex penalty term to guarantee the sparsity of the signal. In order to efficiently solve the cost function model with minimum non-convex and nonsmooth, reduce the computational complexity of the objective function and improve the processing ability of high-dimensional data, in this paper, the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) is used to solve the cost function model. The appropriate p and q values are selected via numerical simulation experiments to achieve the optimal reconstruction accuracy and robustness of sparse signals in SαS noise. The reconstruction probability of sparse signals and image recovery performance are analyzed under the optimal p and q values. The simulation results show that LpLq-ADMM algorithm has great noise suppression ability to SαS noise, and its Peak Signal to Noise Ratio (PSNR) and signal recovery probability is higher than other recovery algorithms.

articleTitle: A Beam-slant Monopole Yagi-Uda Antenna with the Novel Fan-shaped Reflector
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In order to improve the VSWR of the Yagi-Uda antenna operated at 7GHz-11GHz, a monopole Yagi-Uda antenna with a novel fan-shaped reflector is introduced to further solve low VSWR caused by the column reflector. The introduction of the fan-shaped reflector changes the radiation impedance and improves the impedance matching at feed. According to the simulated and tested results, the main beam-slant of about 30° and -10dB bandwidth of more than 3GHz are satisfied over the operated frequencies. Meanwhile, E plane pattern is greater than 5dB gain beamwidth of 45 degrees, and the beam width is greater than the gain of 5dB H map surface direction is 90 degrees.

articleTitle: A High-Performance, Flexible Data Acquisition Library for Radio Instruments
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: The next generation of radio instruments will generate an unprecedented amount of data, with the Square Kilometre Array (SKA) predicted to generate approximately 160 TB of raw data per second. The computational resources required to process this data are considerable, and alongside this challenge there is an associated one: How is this data going to be transported efficiently? Compute servers composing the processing backends of these instruments must be capable of receiving a high data throughput, with enough leftover resources to perform the required computations. In this paper we present a high-performance and flexible library for packet acquisition. This library was developed as part of the effort to prototype a single Low Frequency Aperture Array (LFAA) station, the low frequency component of the SKA. This resulting LFAA demonstrator, the Aperture Array Verification System (AAVS), generates several types of data streams which must be received and processed. The data acquisition (DAQ) library was designed to be capable of receiving and processing multiple data stream types simultaneously whilst minimizing system load. We present the philosophy behind the design and implementation of this library, as well as provide some benchmarking results.

articleTitle: Dual-Target Body Model For Device-Free Localization Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: A dual-target model for quantitative evaluation of the influence of two people standing or moving in the surroundings of a radio link is presented here. This physical model, based on the scalar diffraction theory, is able to predict the effects of the attenuation of the electromagnetic (EM) wavefield generated by a RF transmitter caused by the presence of two people standing or moving in the area covered by a radio link. This model allows to relate, for each link, the RSS measurements at the receiver to the position, size and orientation, of two people located in the link area. Unlike complex EM frameworks that cannot be adopted for real-or near real-time applications, the proposed model can be employed for crowd sensing, occupancy estimation and people counting applications for both indoor and outdoor scenarios. In addition, it paves the way to a complete multi-target body model. This novel model toolkit gets over the restrictions of existing simplified multi-body models for DFL applications that exploit linear superposition of single-body effects. The proposed tool is based on the dual knife-edge approach and on a simplified EM body model, but yet effective for DFL applications. Finally, the experimental part shows some preliminary results on the dual-target applications by exploiting RF measurements obtained with WiFi-compliant radio devices working in the 5 GHz band.

articleTitle: Physical Model-based Calibration for Device-Free Radio Localization and Motion Tracking
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Device-Free Localization (DFL) systems employ a wireless network of radio-frequency (RF) nodes to detect the presence, and locate, or track, the position of targets (people or objects) in a monitored area, without requiring the targets to be instrumented or collaborative. DFL algorithms rely on an initial calibration procedure to avoid problems related to the electromagnetic (EM) effects induced by the environment. This calibration phase includes finger-printing measurement steps that require the presence of the targets in known locations, namely landmark points. These steps are typically time consuming and error-prone since each RF node needs to perform several noisy signal measurements for the assessment of body-induced alterations of the radio propagation. Moreover, modifications in the environment involve frequent recalibration runs to maintain a good level of localization accuracy. We present here a novel calibration scheme based on a physical model that predicts the effects of body-induced alterations of the EM field using a small number of the landmark points used to tune the model parameters. The framework is based on the scalar diffraction theory and it is able to predict the Received Signal Strength at the receivers for an assigned position and size of the targets and the geometry of the links.

articleTitle: Improved Extended Min-Sum Algorithm for Non-Binary LDPC Codes Based on Node Reliability
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Low Density Parity Check (LDPC) codes have been widely applied in recent years, and Extended Min-Sum (EMS) decoding algorithm is the most practical algorithm, which has a fairly low computational cost. Due to the great loss in error correction performance of EMS algorithm, in this paper, we establish constraints to obtain reliable nodes while decoding and evaluate the reliability of the nodes. The nodes and information transferred between nodes are processed and optimized according to the reliability of the nodes. High reliability nodes will not be updated in the decoding process while the information of the sub-reliability nodes will be optimized in different situations, thereby improving the decoding accuracy. This algorithm can accelerate the convergence of the algorithm, while the reduced number of update nodes can control the increase of the computation to a certain extent, and maintain the advantage of the low computation quantity of EMS algorithm. Through simulation results and computational analysis, we prove that the improved algorithm has significantly improved error correction performance compared with the traditional EMS algorithm. Under the same conditions, it has completely entered the waterfall area at 3.6dB, and the EMS algorithm has not entered the waterfall area. By comparing the average iteration times of decoding of the two algorithms, the convergence speed of the algorithm can be reflected. Compared with EMS algorithm, the improved algorithm has significantly improved the convergence speed in most areas, which indicates that the processing of sub-reliable nodes accelerates the convergence of the algorithm. Finally, the average update times of the check nodes and variable nodes of the two algorithms are compared respectively. Although the improved algorithm introduces extra processing flow, it speeds up the convergence of the algorithm, and the computational cost of decoding is less expensive.

articleTitle: Winners of the 2019 ICEAA - IEEE APWC Awards
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: The ICEAA - IEEE APWC conferences have established the ICEAA - IEEE APWC Awards to recognize the young scientists who have authored and orally presented the best papers at the ICEAA - IEEE APWC 2019 joint conferences in terms of content and impact on Electromagnetics. The persons eligible for these awards are young scientists aged not more than thirty-six as of June 3, 2019. The ICEAA - IEEE APWC Awards are administered by the ICEAA Scientific Committee. The ICEAA – IEEE APWC Best Paper Award was awarded to Orestis Christogeorgos for the paper "Design of fully-planar CSRR-based substrateintegrated waveguide circuits" co-authored by and M.-T. Passia, M. Nitas, T.V. Yioultsis, and Vinay Killamsetty for the paper "Exploiting the properties of metagratings for designing rectangular waveguide mode converters" and co-authored by A. Epstein. The announcement and presentation of the award were made at the ICEAA – IEEE APWC 2019 banquet on September 11, 2019, where the winner received a certificate and a prize of 400 Euro donated by the ICEAA Organizing Committee. The IEEE AP-S Industrial Initiatives Committee have established the 2019 ICEAA Industrial Engineering Paper Award to recognize the most innovative paper in terms of practical, industrial engineering related to the fields of antennas, electromagnetics and propagation. The 2019 ICEAA Industrial Engineering Paper Award is administered by the ICEAA Scientific Committee together with IEEE AP-S Industrial Initiatives Committee. The 2019 ICEAA Industrial Engineering Paper Award was awarded to Alejandro Niembro-Martin for the paper "New architecture for wireless 230V powered products based on isolated microstrip line" and co-authored by E. Dreina. The announcement and presentation of the award was made at the ICEAA – IEEE APWC 2019 banquet on September 11, 2019, where the winner received a certificate and a prize of 500 Euro donated by the IEEE AP-S Industrial Initiatives Committee.
